title: [Decision] Is actionLayout (header buttons pinned / More, per list and record) a ruled exception to ADR-0085 §2's re-arrange rule?
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

## 维护者速读
- 要你定什么：页头按钮的「固定/更多」排列写在对象上，分「列表」「记录」两组。这和一条老规定冲突：那条规定说对象上不放「只调整显示顺序」的设置。请你确认这算第二个明确例外（第一个是记录页子表标签的顺序）。
- 现状：功能已经做完，测试全绿，按你 11 月 22 日说的「放在对象上，分列表和记录」做的；审核要求先把例外记进规定，才能合入。
- 席位推荐 A，确认例外：不动代码，只补规定里的一条说明；改名（B）或改到单页设置里（C）都要返工，C 还违背你当时的原话。

## [Decision] Is `actionLayout` (header buttons pinned / More, per list and record scope) a ruled exception to ADR-0085 §2's "re-arrange" sentence?

Card: #36366 (p1, in flight, PR #36629 at head `6303c52011b85208bd7e56d9f6a1a539eb0bd81e`). Raised by the contract-tier L2 record 7092397237 (l2-review#4, finding S1). Drafted by the #36366 card thread for seat repo:objectstack#2.

### Problem in one sentence
An administrator can now choose which header buttons are shown and in what order, for an object's list page and its record page; the platform's own design rule says an object must not carry a setting that only re-arranges what is shown, and only one exception has been ruled so far.

### Background
- The maintainer's words on the format, relayed by seat 7: 2026-11-22T14:27Z 「放在对象上,分列表和记录」 and 14:33Z 「三类都由动作声明,分两步做」 (seat ruling amendment 7080672229); 14:50Z 「#36366 改成"列表"和"记录"两组，每组分"固定"和"更多"两段，等 #36363 合并后，卡标记为p1，剩余任务放回队列」 (release 7087101113).
- Built shape: `ObjectSchema.actionLayout: { list?: Arm, record?: Arm }`, `Arm = { pinned: string[] (≤ 3), more?: string[] }`; optional, no default; an object without it draws as today.
- Readers today (L2 record 7092397237, measured on the head): the `record` arm is read by the record page header, the side preview and the phone's bottom bar (`RecordDetailView.tsx`, `containers.tsx`); the `list` arm by the list page toolbar only (`objectViewPageHeader.tsx`). The row menu / right-click (#36494) and a `selection` arm (#36496) are queued, not built.

### Governing text
- ADR-0085 §2, line 68 at main `3110de5a03` (`docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md`): "Keys that merely hide/re-arrange correct information (`hideRelatedTab`, `showReferenceRail`, `relatedLayout`, `useFieldGroups`, explicit `detail.sections`, or a **modal-vs-page presentation surface** such as a `recordSurface` key) are rejected at this layer. The supported path for per-page control is the one that already exists and is honestly scoped: an **assigned page** (full page schema)."
- ADR-0085 §2, the 2026-11-20 note (#35897 / #35899): "This is the one place §2's "keys that merely hide/re-arrange correct information are rejected at this layer" yields, by that ruling … The guard keeps its force for every other key".
- Admission tests (§2): 1. business intent not inferable from the schema; 2. bound to the object across surfaces, no page name in the key's honest name.
- Re-check: `git show origin/main:docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md | sed -n '61,68p;80,104p'`

Protocol: `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Not yet published; any change of name or placement is free until the first release that carries it.

### Premises (each with its re-check)
1. The key is on no published release yet. Re-check: `git log origin/main --oneline -S'actionLayout' -- packages/spec/src | head` (expect empty until #36629 merges).
2. The `list` arm has one reader today. Re-check: `git grep -n "actionLayout" origin/claude/project-thread-m619um -- 'ui/packages/**/*.tsx' ':!*.test.*'`.
3. Usage pull in the repo's own apps: actions placed at `list_toolbar` in 3 files (5 hits), at `record_header` in 4 files (14 hits), at `record_more` in 3 files (6 hits), under `examples/**` and `packages/apps/**` at main `3110de5a03`. Re-check: `for l in list_toolbar record_header record_more; do git grep -c "'$l'" origin/main -- 'examples/**' 'packages/apps/**' ':!*.test.*'; done`

### Options

| | What is done | What a customer sees | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — ruled exception | Keep the key as built. The weekly ADR PR (#36086) adds a dated note to §2 quoting the maintainer's ruling, saying `actionLayout` is the second ruled exception to the re-arrange sentence (with the `list` arm's single surface stated) and amending "the one place"; the key's jsdoc cites that note. | The admin's 「页头按钮」 panel ships as built: list and record arrangements, saved for everyone. | No code change beyond one jsdoc sentence in PR #36629; one row in the weekly ADR PR. Precedent: #35923 (the `relatedLists` exception note). |
| B — rename the arms | Rename `list` / `record` to names that do not read as pages (e.g. by action scope), and drop the `listPage` / `recordPage` aliases; still needs an ADR note, because the key still only re-arranges. | Same panel; authors write different words. | One patch round on PR #36629 (spec, lint, fold, UI reader, docs, generated baselines); no precedent measured. Does not by itself clear §2's re-arrange sentence. |
| C — move to the assigned-page layer | Remove the object key; the record header pins live in an authored record page's `page:header` (`actions` + `maxVisible`), which means materialising the default page; the list header needs a new list-view carrier. | The admin's arrangement freezes the record page layout it is saved on; list and record are stored in two different places. Seat ruling 7077698148 rejected this route. | Rebuild most of PR #36629 (≈3,500 lines today) plus a new list-view key; no precedent measured. Contradicts 「放在对象上」. |

Business meaning: A is "the header layout is a property of the object, like the order of its related tabs"; B is the same thing under another name; C is "each page remembers its own buttons", which is how a page builder works, not how this design-mode panel was asked for.

### Four axes (business view)
- **Long-term soundness (≥50%).** Two years out, an object's actions will be arranged per action scope (list toolbar + row menu + selection bar for `list`/`selection`; record header + preview + phone bar for `record`), which is where #36494 and #36496 take the `list` scope. A per-scope key on the object is that end state; the guard §2 protects (no per-page show/hide switches) keeps its force. C stores one decision in two places and freezes page layouts. Recall, not measured here: Salesforce keeps list-view buttons per object (search layouts) and record actions on page layouts; Twenty's layout customisation edits per object. A matches the object-level half and the maintainer's ruling.
- **Real business pull.** The maintainer asked for this panel (epic #36359, board 49) and ruled the format; the repo's own apps place 25 actions across the three locations the key arranges. The `list` arm's second surface is queued (#36494), not present.
- **Preventing AI mistakes.** The key is closed (strict arms, at most 3 pinned, named refusals at every door, CLI reference check). With A, the ADR stops saying the opposite of the schema, so an agent reading ADR-0085 is not told to refuse a valid key. B and C add churn with no stronger guard.
- **Startup focus.** A ships what is built and adds one ADR note; B and C spend a rebuild on wording or storage that no customer sees.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term: A keeps one per-scope key on the object, the end state #36494/#36496 extend; C splits one decision across two carriers — favours A.
② Business pull: maintainer-requested panel (epic #36359), format ruled 2026-11-22; 25 placed actions in the repo's apps; list arm single-surface today — favours A.
③ AI mistakes: closed shape with loud refusals either way; A removes the ADR/schema contradiction — favours A.
④ Startup focus: A adds no code; B/C rebuild for no visible gain — favours A.
Prior rulings read: actionlayout,pinnedactions → 0 hits; ADR-0085 §2 + its 2026-11-20 note; thread: 7077698148, 7080672229, 7087101113 (maintainer 14:50Z), L2 7092397237

### Recommendation
**A.** By axis ① alone: one per-scope key on the object is the end state the queued #36494/#36496 build on, and the maintainer already placed it 「放在对象上,分列表和记录」. Self-check: only ① chooses A; ②③④ do not flip it.
Confidence gaps: the `list` arm's second surface is not built yet; the platform comparisons above are from recall, not measured.
Not B: a rename does not change that the key only re-arranges, so it still needs the same exception. Not C: it rebuilds the PR, freezes record layouts and contradicts the maintainer's placement.

### After the ruling
- A: the card thread rewords #36086 row 1 (comment 7091884833) to a ruled exception quoting the maintainer, and the jsdoc in `object-action-layout.ts` to cite the note; L2 delta on PR #36629; seat hands off for approval.
- B: patch round on PR #36629 with the maintainer's names; then as A for the note.
- C: PR #36629 is closed unmerged, the card is re-planned around the assigned page and a list-view key.

Related: #36366, PR #36629, #36359 (epic), #36494, #36495, #36496, #36086, #35897 / #35923 (the first exception).
